title: Title
notes: Open by positioning the chapter as a methods bridge rather than a catalogue. The common theme is that familiar statistical procedures must be rebuilt around angular distance, surface area, and unit-length fitted values, so every answer remains meaningful on the sphere.

title: Route
notes: Use the route slide to make the chapter feel organized around repeated design obligations. Each topic has an ordinary Euclidean ancestor, but the directional version changes the diagnostic, the uncertainty report, or the normalization check.

title: Method Contract
notes: Before moving into individual methods, establish the quality-control rule. A tangent-plane calculation can be useful locally, but the final object must be a direction, cone, density, or curve on the sphere, with a check that makes the constraint visible.

title: Outlier Influence
notes: Explain that outliers on the sphere are not points with unusual magnitude, because every observation has unit length. The diagnostic question is how much one direction changes the resultant vector, either by rotating the fitted mean direction or by shortening the concentration summary.

title: Influence Sweep
notes: Use this slide as a mental version of the notebook's contaminant sweep. Students should learn to ask which observation would change the direction estimate if removed, and which observation mostly reduces the evidence for concentration without rotating the pole much.

title: Robust Direction
notes: Present the robust estimator as an algorithm with a geometric loss, not as a black-box replacement for the mean. The cutoff has an angular interpretation, and the normalization step is part of the definition rather than an afterthought.

title: Bootstrap Cone
notes: Emphasize that the bootstrap preserves the original sample space by resampling directions, not coordinates from a tangent chart unless a tangent method has been explicitly justified. The uncertainty summary is angular, so the final report is immediately readable on the sphere.

title: Bootstrap Workflow
notes: Walk through the workflow slowly because it prevents two common mistakes. Learners should see that resampling happens among the original directions, and that the bootstrap distribution is summarized by angles away from the fitted pole rather than by separate coordinate standard errors.

title: Spherical KDE
notes: Introduce spherical kernel density estimation by comparing it with ordinary KDE only at the conceptual level. The important directional feature is normalization with respect to surface area, so the map and the sphere view are both representations of the same curved density.

title: Bandwidth Tradeoff
notes: Frame bandwidth choice as a scientific judgment with numerical checks, not as a purely aesthetic preference. A directional density estimate should reveal stable angular structure while still integrating properly and agreeing with the visible scatter pattern.

title: Bayesian Shrinkage
notes: Treat the Bayesian material as a geometric doorway. Without deriving a full posterior, students can understand why a prior direction and prior strength act like a pseudo-resultant that shrinks the sample mean toward a stated directional belief.

title: Prior Strength
notes: Ask the audience to read the plot as a robustness check for the prior. A good report does not merely state that a Bayesian estimate was used; it explains how many degrees the answer moved as the prior pseudo-count became more influential.

title: Spherical Smoothing
notes: Connect smoothing to regression without flattening the response. The fitted curve can be computed through ambient weighted averages, but the final curve has to be renormalized, and model quality should be stated in angular residuals along the sphere.

title: Method Audit
notes: This slide translates the notebook's numerical sanity checks into habits students can use in their own projects. Modern methods are flexible, so the audit trail matters: every flexible choice should be paired with a geometry-preserving invariant.

title: Pitfalls
notes: Use the pitfalls slide as a practical warning before the recap. The mistakes all share the same structure: a familiar method is applied in coordinates, but the report forgets to return to angular quantities, surface-area normalization, or unit-norm fitted values.

title: Recap
notes: Close by asking learners to identify the geometric object that each modern method returns. If they can name the object and its invariant check before computing, they are much less likely to turn directional methodology into ordinary multivariate statistics with a spherical picture attached.
